chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh, may Allah be pleased with him, told us: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim told us, from his father, from Dawud ibn Sulayman, from Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

Allah, Exalted and Glorious, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, a servant from among My servants will come to Me with one good deed, and I will make him enter Paradise.' He said: 'O Lord, and what is that good deed?' He said: 'That he relieves a believer from his anguish, even if by (the amount of) a date.' Dawud (peace be upon him) then said: 'It is truly (a must) upon the one who knows You that he does not stop his hope from You.'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific good deed that guarantees entry into Paradise according to the revelation to Dawud?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Mani al-Akhbar* through the chain of the Imams, this hadith highlights the immense spiritual weight of alleviating a believer's distress, emphasizing that even a modest act like giving a date can suffice. It underscores the Shia theological principle that true gnosis of God (*ma'rifah*) naturally cultivates an enduring hope (*rajā'*) in His mercy, linking practical charity directly to eschatological success.
